reason: Verified in Chromium against the built master; I tried hard to kill this and could not. The mechanism is exactly as stated. At 1440x960 owner-flight .b-plan is clientHeight 664 over scrollHeight 1727 - 1063px (62%) below the fold - and only two of the seven moments (Menu tasting, Send the invitations) sit inside the pane; item three starts at y=948 against a fold at 894.9. Computed maskImage and webkitMaskImage are 'none' on both .b-plan and .b-stick at every desk size, getComputedStyle(el,'::before'/'::after').content is 'none' on both, scrollbarGutter is 'auto', and offsetWidth-clientWidth measures 0, so nothing at all - not even a reserved gutter - marks the edge. The slicing reproduces: at 1366x768 the fold at 702.9 cuts 'Send the invitations' (694.3-725.3, 28% shown), its count '23' (21% shown) and the 'days away' unit mid-glyph; at 1280x800 it halves 'Sat 8 Aug' (49%); at 1024x700 it halves the .b-grab 'Edit' (51%) and at 1920x1080 the same control (65%). I clicked the visible half of that 'Edit' at 1024x700 at y=628 against a fold at 634.9 and it opened the editor - a control the owner can press but cannot see. A cropped screenshot at 1366x768 shows the letter-tops of 'Send the invitations' hanging over an unbroken full-width footer hairline; it reads as a rendering fault, not as 'more below'. The top edge is real too: in owner-undone the plan is programmatically at scrollTop 307, the rail's stroke begins hard at the pane lip (rail top -18.7 vs pane top 230.9), and the 'days away' measure head (-56) and the 'Today, 16 July' origin (-25) are gone with no sign they exist. Two supporting numbers in the finding are loose and neither changes the verdict: the rail's blank tail at 1440x960 measures 326px/49%, not 337px/51%; and the sliced half-line sits 40.1px above the closing footer rule at every size I measured, not 4-20px. The gates do not cover this - interaction-check.mjs contains no fade, mask or fold-edge assertion and only ever uses the pane's overflow to drive a scroll - so it restates nothing already proven, and lessons.md line 86 names this class verbatim ('never an always-on decoration, never a mid-word slice'), newly reintroduced by round 8's frame. The brief's suggested kill - that the fix is decoration - fails on its own terms: --fadeTop/--fadeBot default to 0px and are raised only by data-fade written after measuring scrollTop and scrollHeight-clientHeight-scrollTop, which is precisely the 'measured after layout' the library demands. I simulated the exact proposed CSS plus the measuring pass in the live page across owner-flight, owner-undone and owner-editing: pane rects, widths, scrollHeight, clientHeight and scrollTop are byte-identical before and after (no layout shift), there are no fixed or sticky descendants inside either pane for the mask's new containing block to re-anchor, the .b-edit undo bar keeps its exact rect, and the attribute proves itself honest - .b-stick carries no data-fade in owner-flight where nothing is hidden, gains 'bottom' the moment the editor makes it overflow, and .b-plan carries 'top bottom' in owner-undone. The rendered result fades '15 August 2026' out of the rail instead of guillotining it. No new hue, no new weight, no architectural change.
sharpenedFix: Ship the fix as proposed, with three tightenings. (1) Add scroll-padding-block: 40px to both panes at >=1024. Chromium's focus scrolling lands a control flush against the scroll-container edge - i.e. inside the new fade - so without it a Tab through the plan will park an 'Edit' or a stepper under the very gradient that is meant to say 'this is on its way out', dimming a focused control and its ring. With it, focus always stops clear of the band. (2) Set scrollbar-gutter: stable alongside the existing scrollbar-width: thin on .b-stick. The rail measures scrollHeight 664 (no overflow) in owner-flight and 925 in owner-undone/owner-editing, so opening the editor makes the rail scrollable and, on a platform with classic scrollbars, shifts the whole horizon column sideways at the exact instant the owner is reading it. The finding is right that no gutter is reserved; that is the concrete cost of it. (3) Drive the measuring pass off one shared helper called from the pane's rAF-throttled scroll handler, from the end of every repaint, and from the resize handler, and have it removeAttribute('data-fade') when nothing is hidden - never leave a stale attribute behind a repaint that shortened the content, or the fade becomes the decoration the library forbids. Keep the band at 40px: it is roughly one row's cap-to-descender, enough to read as a soft edge and short enough that no fully-visible row is dimmed.
